facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable for a credit snapshot, with the limits stated below. Everything rests on filed, consolidated statements of Entegris, Inc. and subsidiaries in USD millions, supplemented by the company's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA, which the filings reconcile to GAAP. On that basis, principal debt fell from $4,045.0 at FY2024 to $3,745.0 at FY2025 and $3,295.0 at September 26, 2026, while LTM Adjusted EBITDA rose from $886.2 (FY2025) to $1,008.2, so total debt over Adjusted EBITDA moved from 4.34x to 4.23x to 3.27x. The nine-month 2026 debt reduction is entirely term loan B repayment of $450.0; every remaining instrument is a fixed-rate note, the revolver is undrawn, and maturities start in 2028. Interest cover on cash interest paid is 5.57x LTM. Three things restrict the view. First, Adjusted EBITDA is management-defined and the covenant definition is not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable; the filing states compliance and a 5.20 to 1.00 first lien net leverage maximum that is tested only above a revolver utilisation threshold that is not printed. Second, letters of credit under the revolver are not supplied, so undrawn availability is shown before them. Third, 2026 operating income and margin are not like-for-like with 2025 because of the January 2026 change in useful lives, while Adjusted EBITDA adds depreciation back and is unaffected by it. The annual report's thousands captions on millions amounts are a known unit-label conflict, resolved by the Q3 10-Q statement that amounts are in millions (10-K page:120, Q3 10-Q page:9).

facts.label: Covenants
facts.text: The credit agreement for the revolver and term loan (the "Amended Credit Agreement") contains a maximum first lien net leverage ratio of 5.20 to 1.00, tested only when utilisation of the revolver exceeds a specified threshold; the company states compliance through September 26, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:34; same wording in Q2 10-Q page:31; Q1 10-Q page:28 states compliance without a level). The threshold is not printed, the reported ratio is not printed, and no step-down is described. The revolver margin tiers depend on the same first lien net leverage ratio, and the margin fell from 1.50% (SOFR) at June 27, 2026 to 1.25% at September 26, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:12; Q3 10-Q page:12), which is consistent with improving first lien leverage but does not give the ratio. An illustrative figure only: if the 1,600.0 secured notes are first lien debt and cash is fully netted, first lien net debt over LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 1.23x (C8); the covenant definition of debt, cash netting and EBITDA are not supplied, so this is not covenant headroom and no headroom is stated. Other restrictions are summarised in the annual report risk factors: restrictions on debt, dividends, investments, liens and asset sales, and incremental capacity up to the greater of $1.1 billion or 100% of EBITDA plus amounts subject to a secured net leverage test (10-K page:54); the indentures carry limited covenants on secured debt, sale-leasebacks and restricted subsidiary debt (10-K page:56).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The business context is usable, with a clear picture of what the company does and a thin picture of who owns it and what it has contracted. Entegris sells consumable materials and purity equipment into semiconductor fabrication through two segments, Materials Solutions and Advanced Purity Solutions, and describes its revenue as predominantly unit-driven or recurring (management language, 10-K page:9). The mechanism that matters to a creditor is demand linkage: sales follow wafer starts and fab build-outs, a few very large customers account for half of sales, and customers carry no long-term purchase commitments, so revenue visibility is short and a cut in one customer's capital plan transmits quickly into volume, operating leverage and debt service. The latest quarter shows the upside of that link: Q3 2026 net sales grew 24.6% on volume, but the equipment-linked customer category grew far faster than fabs, which is the more cyclical part of the mix. On ownership and transactions, the pack shows a publicly traded company with 907 holders of record, no sponsor, no parent, no acquisition disclosed and no new debt issue; the transaction history is a portfolio clean-up between 2023 and 2025 whose asset sales coincided with large debt repayments, and the 2026 financing events are an amended revolver and repayment of the term loan from cash flow. What the pack cannot show is who the large holders are, what the financing documents permit beyond summaries, and how the company is rated.

What the pack cannot show is who the large holders are, what the financing documents permit beyond summaries, and how the company is rated.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: There is no sponsor transaction, acquisition, merger, recapitalisation or new debt issue in the supplied sources for 2026, and none is announced by the as-of date. The financing events in 2026 are two. First, on April 29, 2026 the company amended its senior secured revolving credit facility to raise commitments to $750.0 million from $575.0 million, extend the maturity to April 29, 2031 from July 6, 2027, and revise margins, commitment fees and certain negative covenants (Q3 10-Q page:12, page:22); the revised negative covenants are not described, and the amendment itself is not supplied. Second, the company repaid the term loans B in full during 2026 (50.0 in the first quarter, 200.0 in the second and 200.0 in the third, including a voluntary 25 on July 31, 2026), so that outstanding principal is now only fixed-rate notes of $3,295.0 million and an undrawn revolver (Q1 10-Q page:11; Q2 10-Q page:12, page:17; Q3 10-Q page:11, page:12). Cash flow statements for the nine months show repayments of $450.0 million and no proceeds from new long-term debt (Q3 10-Q page:7); the revolver was borrowed and repaid at 65.0 during the period. For use of proceeds and liquidity effect, the repayments were funded from operating cash flow of $606.0 million over nine months and reduced cash by little (cash $356.5 million against $360.4 million at December 31, 2025). Earlier history that shaped the balance sheet: the CMC Materials acquisition closed in July 2022 and was financed under the July 2022 credit agreement amendment and indenture supplements listed as exhibits (10-K page:5, page:97); debt payments of $848.3 million against proceeds of $224.5 million in FY2024 and payments of $300.0 million in FY2025 came after the asset sales listed in the timeline (10-K page:108). The nature of the FY2024 long-term debt proceeds is not described in the pack beyond a third amendment of the term loan facility in 2024 (10-K page:76, page:98). The dividend declared on October 14, 2026 ($0.10 per share, payable November 18, 2026) is a subsequent event after the quarter end (Q3 10-Q page:17). Management's Capital Markets Day on November 9, 2026 is a future event after the as-of date and no content from it is available (Q3 release page:1).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Entegris, Inc. is a cyclical, customer-concentrated supplier of semiconductor materials whose credit profile improved sharply in 2026 and is now adequate for its debt load. The strongest support is deleveraging with cash generation: total debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 3.27x on an LTM Q3 2026 basis against 4.23x for FY2025, the term loan has been repaid, the remaining USD 3,295.0 million of debt is fixed-rate notes, and nothing matures before 2028. The weakest point is the quality and durability of earnings: demand is volume-led from a few very large customers with no purchase commitments, and 2026 margins are helped by an accounting change and one-off refunds. What decides the outcome is whether advanced logic and memory fab demand holds through the 2028 to 2030 maturities. [CP-1 leverage data; CP-1A operating model]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The first finding is that Entegris, Inc. has deleveraged on both sides of the ratio. Par debt fell to USD 3,295.0 million at September 26, 2026 from USD 3,745.0 million at December 31, 2025 through term loan repayment of USD 450.0 million, while LTM Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 1,008.2 million from USD 886.2 million in FY2025, so total debt over Adjusted EBITDA moved from 4.34x at FY2024 to 4.23x at FY2025 and 3.27x LTM Q3 2026, and net debt over Adjusted EBITDA from 3.99x to 3.82x to 2.91x. The mechanism is repayment from operating cash flow, which also removed floating-rate exposure, so the remaining debt service is fixed coupons of about USD 161.3 million a year and cash interest cover is 5.57x. [CP-1 leverage and interest cover data, debt schedule]

If capital spending returns toward the roughly USD 250.0 million planned in the annual report, or payables normalise, free cash flow would fall. [CP-1 financials and cash flow quality]

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Debt reduction with falling leverage is a documented fact: total debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 3.27x LTM Q3 2026, down from 4.34x at FY2024, with all remaining debt fixed-rate notes and no maturity before 2028 (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 leverage data and debt schedule). Cash generation is strong: LTM free cash flow of USD 616.0 million exceeds the sum of the roughly USD 161.3 million of annual note coupons and LTM dividends of USD 61.3 million, which is USD 222.6 million, by USD 393.4 million (Analyst Interpretation of CP-1 cash flow figures; the coupon figure excludes revolver fees). Liquidity of USD 1,106.5 million before letters of credit, with no facility expiring within twelve months, gives room to absorb a downturn (Documentary Fact for the inputs; the sum excludes unsupplied letters of credit). The business is embedded in customer processes through recurring consumables and no platform exceeds 3% of net sales, which management describes as supporting revenue that is predominantly unit-driven or recurring (Management Language; basis CP-1A operating model). Capital allocation is creditor-friendly on documented actions: debt repayment, steady dividends and no repurchases, with no sponsor (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A governance).

rows.label: Entegris is a cyclical, concentrated but strongly cash-generative supplier whose credit profile improved in 2026: leverage on par debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 3.27x LTM Q3 2026 and nothing matures before 2028. The gain depends on demand holding.
Leverage fell from 4.23x at FY2025 to 3.27x on an LTM Q3 2026 basis, with net debt over Adjusted EBITDA at 2.91x.
LTM Q3 2026 free cash flow was $616.0 million and cash interest cover was 5.57x; the remaining notes carry about $161.3 million of annual coupons.
Cash is $356.5 million and the undrawn revolver is $750.0 million before letters of credit; $2,000.0 million, or 60.7% of par debt, matures in 2029.
TSMC was 16% of FY2025 net sales, the top ten customers were 50%, and customers have no long-term purchase commitments.
2026 margins are lifted by lower depreciation and tariff refunds; on unadjusted EBITDA, leverage is 3.36x rather than 3.27x.
Demand reversal in advanced logic, memory and fab construction

spans.text: ## Request

Issuer: ENTEGRIS INC (Entegris, Inc., Delaware registrant, NASDAQ: ENTG; issuer id entg). As-of date: 2026-11-05; evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit snapshot. Reporting currency: USD; the filings report in US dollars, in millions except per-share data. Requested scope: can the seven supplied filings and releases support the follow-on work (financial data extraction, business and transaction context, fundamental credit synthesis and evidence-trace review), and what stays blocked. Current period is the quarter ended September 26, 2026 (Q3 2026) and the prior period is FY2025 (year ended December 31, 2025), as set in the context file. The context file holds the run settings only and is not issuer evidence; it names no borrower, parent, guarantor, sponsor, rating, quote or deal term, and none of those blank fields is treated as zero.

This module gives a source-readiness view only. It makes no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no new financial calculation (the method forbids normalizing or reconciling figures at this stage).
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on

Each file is a text extraction of an EDGAR HTML document, split into numbered chunks. A `page:N` locator below means chunk N of that extraction, not the printed page. The sha256 is the pack file hash that CP-OS pinned. The first line of each chunk 1 carries a different hash, which is the hash of the original HTML document and not of the pack file.
| Source (exact name) | sha256 | Chunks |

Run settings (not issuer evidence): `context`, sha256 `a75dcef49bab6da60dc1054c04d1bf4409ccb60667119c9ab2f0bfc98a4c262f`. The file `_retrieval.json` in the pack folder was ignored by CP-OS and is not used.
### Upstream handoffs
None. CP-0 is the first module of this run; CP-OS supplied no handoff.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven supplied filings and releases are sufficient for a credit snapshot of Entegris, with limitations. Statements, debt, segment and liquidity data through September 26, 2026 are located. Legal financing documents and covenant calculations are not supplied. | Medium | Executed credit agreement and indentures, revolver letters of credit, the covenant test threshold and guarantor details are not in the pack. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| The latest debt note lists par debt of $3,295.0 million and no revolver borrowings at September 26, 2026. | Debt and maturity analysis can proceed from filed statements. | High |

| Annual report notes are captioned in thousands but show millions; the latest quarterly report says amounts are in millions. | Treat all amounts as USD millions and flag the caption conflict. | High |

| Revolver commitments are $750.0 million, but letters of credit and the threshold for the 5.20 to 1.00 leverage covenant are not printed. | Net revolver availability and covenant headroom cannot be calculated from the pack. | High |

| Quarterly results for the first three quarters of 2026 and prior-year comparatives are in the filings and releases. | Quarter, year-to-date and last-twelve-month views can be built from filed figures. | High |
| A January 2026 change in useful lives cut depreciation by $55.6 million over nine months. | Operating income and margin comparisons with 2025 are affected. | High |
### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested work with bounded limitations; the overall view is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. The pack holds one audited annual report (FY2025), three unaudited quarterly reports (Q1 to Q3 2026) and three earnings releases, all for one reporting entity, Entegris, Inc. and subsidiaries on a consolidated basis. Filed statements control financial facts; the earnings releases are management documents that supply attributed non-GAAP measures and the fourth-quarter outlook, and they do not override the filings. No source is blocked, no extraction failure was seen, and no draft or unsigned document is in the pack. Each filing carries a signature block and the annual report carries an unqualified auditor opinion. The limits come from what the pack omits: no executed financing document, no covenant calculation, no letter-of-credit figure and no guarantor schedule. These bound the debt-terms, liquidity-headroom and creditor-structure work but do not stop it.
| Downstream owner | Readiness | Evidence supplied | Bounded limitation |

| CP-1 financial data | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Statements, debt note, maturities, cash flow, segments and interim comparatives (see source review) | Letters of credit, covenant threshold and ratio, and interim lease detail are not supplied |

| CP-1A business and transaction context | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Annual business description, risk factors, segment and customer-concentration text, quarterly narrative, October 2026 release | No sponsor, parent, deal terms or ownership document; the context file names none |

| CP-5 evidence trace review | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Pack text for quote checks | Inherits the unit-caption conflict and the gaps below |

| Ref | Conflict or distinction | Locators | Downstream effect |

| C1 | The annual report captions debt maturities, fair value and lease tables "(In thousands)", but the values (for example total debt $3,745.0) match the millions used in the statements. The Q3 10-Q says the thousands captions were wrong, the amounts are millions and no revision is needed. | `10-K page:120`, `page:122`, `page:123`; `10-Q Q3 page:9` | Treat every amount as USD millions. CP-1 should record the caption conflict and not scale values. |

The reporting entity is Entegris, Inc. with its subsidiaries; the filings present consolidated figures only. The annual exhibit list names "certain subsidiaries" as parties to the notes indentures and as guarantors under the 2022 credit agreement amendment (`10-K page:97`), but no guarantor list, restricted or unrestricted subsidiary split, or subsidiary schedule is supplied in text. spans.text: ## Request

Issuer: ENTEGRIS INC (Entegris, Inc. and subsidiaries, consolidated; NASDAQ: ENTG; issuer id entg). As-of date: 2026-11-05; evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit snapshot. Reporting currency: USD; all filed amounts are in USD millions except per-share data. Current period: Q3 2026 (quarter ended September 26, 2026) and the last twelve months to that date (LTM Q3 2026); prior period: FY2025 (year ended December 31, 2025), with FY2024 as the earlier year.

Task: extract the financial base for the credit snapshot from the supplied filings and releases: statements, debt and maturity profile, liquidity, leverage, interest cover and cash flow, with the definition review and the gaps that restrict use. Source abbreviations used in locators: `10-K` (annual report FY2025), `Q1 10-Q`, `Q2 10-Q`, `Q3 10-Q` (quarterly reports for the quarters ended March 28, June 27 and September 26, 2026), `Q1 release`, `Q2 release`, `Q3 release` (earnings releases, Exhibit 99.1, dated April 30, August 4 and October 29, 2026). `page:N` is the chunk number of the pinned extraction, not the printed page.

Perimeter and basis. The issuer is the registrant itself, so the consolidated statements are the issuer's own statements and no parent or subsidiary substitution applies. Accounting basis: US GAAP; Adjusted EBITDA is the company's own non-GAAP measure (defined in the Definition review). "LTM Q3 2026" means FY2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025, with each input shown in Calculations. Debt in leverage ratios is principal (par) outstanding unless stated; carrying value is shown separately.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Leverage on par debt over company-defined Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.34x at FY2024 to 3.27x on an LTM Q3 2026 basis, helped by the term loan repayment and higher earnings. | Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| LTM Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA is $1,008.2 million against $886.2 million for FY2025; net debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 2.91x against 3.82x. | Deleveraging came from higher earnings and lower debt; Adjusted EBITDA is a company-defined measure. | Medium |

| LTM cash interest paid is $181.1 million, giving cover of 5.57x against 4.78x for FY2025; the remaining notes carry about $161.3 million of annual coupons. | Cash interest burden is falling as floating-rate debt is repaid, which supports debt service. | Medium |

### Financial base view

The financial base is usable for a credit snapshot, with the limits stated below. Everything rests on filed, consolidated statements of Entegris, Inc. and subsidiaries in USD millions, supplemented by the company's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA, which the filings reconcile to GAAP. On that basis, principal debt fell from $4,045.0 at FY2024 to $3,745.0 at FY2025 and $3,295.0 at September 26, 2026, while LTM Adjusted EBITDA rose from $886.2 (FY2025) to $1,008.2, so total debt over Adjusted EBITDA moved from 4.34x to 4.23x to 3.27x. The nine-month 2026 debt reduction is entirely term loan B repayment of $450.0; every remaining instrument is a fixed-rate note, the revolver is undrawn, and maturities start in 2028. Interest cover on cash interest paid is 5.57x LTM. Three things restrict the view. First, Adjusted EBITDA is management-defined and the covenant definition is not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable; the filing states compliance and a 5.20 to 1.00 first lien net leverage maximum that is tested only above a revolver utilisation threshold that is not printed. Second, letters of credit under the revolver are not supplied, so undrawn availability is shown before them. Third, 2026 operating income and margin are not like-for-like with 2025 because of the January 2026 change in useful lives, while Adjusted EBITDA adds depreciation back and is unaffected by it. The annual report's thousands captions on millions amounts are a known unit-label conflict, resolved by the Q3 10-Q statement that amounts are in millions (`10-K page:120`, `Q3 10-Q page:9`).

### Covenants

The credit agreement for the revolver and term loan (the "Amended Credit Agreement") contains a maximum first lien net leverage ratio of 5.20 to 1.00, tested only when utilisation of the revolver exceeds a specified threshold; the company states compliance through September 26, 2026 (`Q3 10-Q page:34`; same wording in `Q2 10-Q page:31`; `Q1 10-Q page:28` states compliance without a level). The threshold is not printed, the reported ratio is not printed, and no step-down is described. The revolver margin tiers depend on the same first lien net leverage ratio, and the margin fell from 1.50% (SOFR) at June 27, 2026 to 1.25% at September 26, 2026 (`Q2 10-Q page:12`; `Q3 10-Q page:12`), which is consistent with improving first lien leverage but does not give the ratio. An illustrative figure only: if the 1,600.0 secured notes are first lien debt and cash is fully netted, first lien net debt over LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 1.23x (C8); the covenant definition of debt, cash netting and EBITDA are not supplied, so this is not covenant headroom and no headroom is stated. Other restrictions are summarised in the annual report risk factors: restrictions on debt, dividends, investments, liens and asset sales, and incremental capacity up to the greater of $1.1 billion or 100% of EBITDA plus amounts subject to a secured net leverage test (`10-K page:54`); the indentures carry limited covenants on secured debt, sale-leasebacks and restricted subsidiary debt (`10-K page:56`).
### Latest quarter and subsequent events

- Debt: the remaining 200.0 of term loans B was repaid in Q3 2026, including a voluntary 25 payment made on July 31, 2026 (`Q2 10-Q page:17`; `Q3 10-Q page:12`); the 25 payment was disclosed as a subsequent event in the Q2 10-Q, and the loss on extinguishment was 1.7 in the quarter and 3.9 over nine months (`Q3 10-Q page:12`).

- Revolver: amended April 29, 2026, with commitments raised to 750.0 from 575.0, maturity extended to April 29, 2031 from July 6, 2027, and revised margins, commitment fees and certain negative covenants (`Q3 10-Q page:12`, `page:22`).

- Operating items: an equity investment impairment of 6.7 (first nine months, recorded in the second quarter per `Q3 release page:9`); restructuring of 11.2 over nine months, including the planned wind-down of Life Sciences Fluid Management (`Q3 10-Q page:16`); 8.3 of IEEPA tariff refunds in Q3 recognised in cost of sales and excluded from non-GAAP results (`Q3 10-Q page:38`).
- Subsequent events: a dividend of $0.10 per share declared October 14, 2026, payable November 18, 2026 (`Q3 10-Q page:17`); no other subsequent event is disclosed.

- Outlook (management expectation, not fact): fourth-quarter 2026 sales of 1,025 to 1,055 and Adjusted EBITDA of 315 to 329 (`Q3 release page:10`); a Capital Markets Day on November 9, 2026 is after the as-of date (`Q3 release page:1`).
### Definition review

- Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income adjusted to exclude equity in net loss of affiliates, income tax expense, interest expense, interest income, other expense net, depreciation and Special Items (`10-K page:83`). It does not list share-based compensation as an adjustment, and the reconciliations show none (`Q3 10-Q page:38`: 54.8 of share-based compensation over nine months stays in Adjusted EBITDA).

- The 2026 nine-month add-backs are restructuring of 11.2 and an IEEPA refund deduction of (8.3), plus amortization of 138.0 and depreciation of 102.4 (`Q3 10-Q page:38`). FY2025 add-backs were restructuring of 29.7 and a loss on business sale of 10.9 (`10-K page:85`).

- The difference between Adjusted EBITDA and unadjusted EBITDA (operating income plus depreciation and amortization) is 40.6 for FY2025 (886.2 less 845.6, equal to restructuring of 29.7 plus the loss on business sale of 10.9), 19.0 for FY2024, 17.4 for nine months 2025 and 2.9 for nine months 2026 (C3), so management adjustments are small and shrinking in 2026.

- The January 2026 useful-life change cut depreciation by 55.6 over nine months 2026 (`Q3 10-Q page:9`); it lifts GAAP operating income and net income but not Adjusted EBITDA, which adds depreciation back.

- The releases net interest income against interest expense ("Interest expense, net" of 43.9 in Q3 2026 in `Q3 release page:5`); this module uses the gross filed lines (45.4 and 1.5 income, `Q3 10-Q page:5`).
- Covenant EBITDA, first lien net debt and the utilisation threshold are not supplied; any comparison with the 5.20 to 1.00 maximum is therefore Not calculable here.
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow was 606.0 in nine months 2026 against 503.4 in nine months 2025, helped by a 266.7 inflow from accounts payable and accrued liabilities that offset outflows of 167.5 in receivables and 153.2 in inventories (`Q3 10-Q page:7`); the working-capital inflow is partly timing of vendor payments and incentive accrual (`Q3 10-Q page:33`), so LTM free cash flow of 616.0 may include timing support. Cash interest paid (90.4 over nine months) is far below gross interest expense (142.9) because accrued interest payable rose to 64.9 from 24.3 (`Q3 10-Q page:4`); the 52.5 gap is mostly that accrual build of 40.6 (C11) plus 9.6 of non-cash amortization of debt costs (`Q3 10-Q page:7`). Net cash used in financing was 486.8, of which 450.0 was term loan repayment and 46.2 dividends (`Q3 10-Q page:7`).
## Calculations
Every input is a filed figure with the locator shown in the tables above. Results are rounded to the precision shown.
| Ref | Calculation | Inputs | Result |
| C1 | LTM Adjusted EBITDA, Q3 2026 | FY2025 886.2 + nine months 2026 780.1 − nine months 2025 658.1 | 1,008.2. Cross-check by quarters: 228.1 + 226.1 + 250.7 + 303.3 = 1,008.2 |
| C1a | LTM Adjusted EBITDA, Q2 2026 | FY2025 886.2 + six months 2026 476.8 − six months 2025 437.4 (`Q2 10-Q page:27`) | 925.6 |
| C1b | Q4 2025 Adjusted EBITDA implied | FY2025 886.2 − nine months 2025 658.1 | 228.1, equal to the printed discrete column in the Q1 release |

| C4 | Free cash flow = operating cash flow less acquisition of property, plant and equipment | FY2024 631.7 − 315.6; FY2025 695.4 − 299.2; nine months 2025 503.4 − 241.2; nine months 2026 606.0 − 124.0; LTM 798.0 − 182.0 | 316.1; 396.2; 262.2; 482.0; 616.0. FCF / par debt: 316.1 / 4,045.0 = 7.8%; 396.2 / 3,745.0 = 10.6%; 616.0 / 3,295.0 = 18.7%. After LTM dividends of 61.3: 554.7 |
| C6 | Liquidity at September 26, 2026 | Cash 356.5 + undrawn commitment 750.0 (750.0 − 0.0 borrowed) | 1,106.5 before letters of credit (Not supplied) |
| C8 | Illustrative first lien net leverage (not covenant) | (secured notes 1,600.0 + revolver 0.0 − cash 356.5) / 1,008.2 | 1.23x; gross 1,600.0 / 1,008.2 = 1.59x |

| C9 | Annual coupon on remaining notes | 1,600.0 × 4.75% + 895.0 × 5.95% + 400.0 × 3.625% + 400.0 × 4.375% = 76.0 + 53.3 + 14.5 + 17.5 | 161.3 (about 4.89% of par); LTM Adjusted EBITDA 1,008.2 / 161.3 = 6.25x, illustrative and excluding revolver fees |
| C10 | Debt change and fair value ratio | Par 3,745.0 − 3,295.0 = 450.0 repaid; fair value 3,176.1 / par 3,295.0 | 450.0 (term loans B); 96.4% |
| C11 | Accrued interest build | 64.9 − 24.3 | 40.6 |
## Gaps
| Ref | Gap | Effect | Action |

| F1 | Covenant EBITDA, first lien net debt definition, the revolver utilisation threshold and the reported covenant ratio are not supplied (searched all sources; only the 5.20 to 1.00 level and a compliance statement are printed). | Covenant headroom is Not calculable. | Obtain the credit agreement and compliance certificate. |

| F2 | Letters of credit under the revolver are not supplied. | Undrawn availability is shown before letters of credit and may be overstated; liquidity of 1,106.5 is an upper bound. | Obtain the letter-of-credit balance. |

| F3 | Guarantors, co-issuers, collateral package and notes maturity months are not supplied in text. | Structural priority and recovery analysis cannot be built beyond instrument labels. | Add the indentures and subsidiary list if needed. |

| F4 | Lease, pension, purchase obligation and tax detail is as of December 31, 2025 only; the interim reports have no such notes. | Those claims are stale by nine months; the Q3 10-Q states no material change in cash requirements outside the term loan repayment (`page:35`). | Label as of December 31, 2025. |

| F5 | The unit-caption conflict in the annual report remains (thousands captions on millions amounts). | Handled by treating all amounts as millions; the pension table has the same caption. | Carry as a stated limitation. |

| F6 | Adjusted EBITDA is management-defined and adds back restructuring and other items; no covenant or lender definition is available. | Leverage and cover are on the company's own definition; unadjusted EBITDA gives 3.36x total leverage LTM Q3 2026. | Show both, as in the metrics table. |
| F7 | The FY2024 revolver commitment at December 31, 2024 is not dated in the pack. | The FY2024 undrawn facility is Not supplied. | None needed for the current view. |

| F8 | Interest paid is lumpy by coupon date and a dash for the first quarter of 2025 appears in the Q1 10-Q, so no LTM Q1 2026 cover ratio is given. | Cover is shown for FY2024, FY2025, LTM Q2 2026 and LTM Q3 2026 only. | None needed. |

| F9 | 2026 operating income and net income are flattered by the useful-life change and tariff refunds; the fourth-quarter outlook is management expectation. | Margin comparison with 2025 is not like-for-like at operating income level. | Use Adjusted EBITDA for trend and flag the change. |
## Next module

Pass to the business and transaction context module with: the readiness limits from CP-0 and this handoff, the leverage path (4.34x FY2024, 4.23x FY2025, 3.27x LTM Q3 2026 on par debt over Adjusted EBITDA), the debt schedule and 2028 to 2030 maturity wall, liquidity of 1,106.5 before letters of credit, and the open gaps F1 to F3 (covenant, letters of credit, guarantor structure). The business module should treat Adjusted EBITDA as management language, use the segment table above for mix (Advanced Purity Solutions profit growth is the main driver), and not describe any sponsor, parent or deal terms, since none are supplied. The synthesis module must not state covenant headroom or net revolver availability, and should flag the useful-life change and the unit-caption conflict wherever 2026 margins or the annual report notes are cited.

Consistency with upstream. This handoff agrees with CP-0 and CP-1 and corrects neither. It uses the CP-1 figures unchanged (par debt $3,295.0 million at September 26, 2026; LTM Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA $1,008.2 million) and carries forward the CP-0 and CP-1 limits: no covenant ratio, no letters of credit, no guarantor schedule.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Entegris is a widely held semiconductor materials supplier with no sponsor or parent identified. Customer concentration and cyclical demand drive business risk, while documented capital allocation favours debt repayment. Transaction evidence is limited to a revolver amendment. | Medium | Financing contracts, holder detail beyond a record count, credit ratings and customer concentration after FY2025 are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| TSMC was 16% of FY2025 net sales and the top ten customers were 50%; customers give non-binding forecasts without long-term purchase commitments. | Revenue visibility is short and concentrated, so one customer's capital plan can move cash flow. | High |

| Q3 2026 net sales rose 24.6% year on year, mainly on volume; Equipment and Engineering sales rose from $115.2 million to $192.1 million. | Growth includes more cyclical equipment-linked demand, which can reverse and weaken margin and leverage gains. | Medium |

| No sponsor, parent or controlling holder is identified; dividends were $0.10 per share each quarter and no shares were repurchased in FY2025. | No sponsor-driven extraction is documented, but legal capacity to distribute cannot be tested without the credit agreement. | Medium |

| The 2026 financing events in the pack are the April 29, 2026 revolver amendment and full term loan repayment; no new notes appear. | Financing activity reduced debt and extended the revolver rather than adding claims. | High |

| Raw materials include single-source inputs, China sales were flat, and $8.3 million of tariff refunds were received in Q3 2026. | Supply and trade shocks can hit margins; the refund is a one-off that lifts reported 2026 margins. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

The business context is usable, with a clear picture of what the company does and a thin picture of who owns it and what it has contracted. Entegris sells consumable materials and purity equipment into semiconductor fabrication through two segments, Materials Solutions and Advanced Purity Solutions, and describes its revenue as predominantly unit-driven or recurring (management language, `10-K page:9`). The mechanism that matters to a creditor is demand linkage: sales follow wafer starts and fab build-outs, a few very large customers account for half of sales, and customers carry no long-term purchase commitments, so revenue visibility is short and a cut in one customer's capital plan transmits quickly into volume, operating leverage and debt service. The latest quarter shows the upside of that link: Q3 2026 net sales grew 24.6% on volume, but the equipment-linked customer category grew far faster than fabs, which is the more cyclical part of the mix. On ownership and transactions, the pack shows a publicly traded company with 907 holders of record, no sponsor, no parent, no acquisition disclosed and no new debt issue; the transaction history is a portfolio clean-up between 2023 and 2025 whose asset sales coincided with large debt repayments, and the 2026 financing events are an amended revolver and repayment of the term loan from cash flow. What the pack cannot show is who the large holders are, what the financing documents permit beyond summaries, and how the company is rated.

| Revenue model | Unit-driven or recurring | In 2025 revenue was predominantly unit-driven or recurring from products consumed in manufacturing; no single product platform exceeded 3% of net sales | Management Language | `10-K page:9`, `page:10` | Supports revenue durability through a downturn if wafer volumes hold; the 3% platform statement is management's, not tested |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

There is no sponsor transaction, acquisition, merger, recapitalisation or new debt issue in the supplied sources for 2026, and none is announced by the as-of date. The financing events in 2026 are two. First, on April 29, 2026 the company amended its senior secured revolving credit facility to raise commitments to $750.0 million from $575.0 million, extend the maturity to April 29, 2031 from July 6, 2027, and revise margins, commitment fees and certain negative covenants (`Q3 10-Q page:12`, `page:22`); the revised negative covenants are not described, and the amendment itself is not supplied. Second, the company repaid the term loans B in full during 2026 (50.0 in the first quarter, 200.0 in the second and 200.0 in the third, including a voluntary 25 on July 31, 2026), so that outstanding principal is now only fixed-rate notes of $3,295.0 million and an undrawn revolver (`Q1 10-Q page:11`; `Q2 10-Q page:12`, `page:17`; `Q3 10-Q page:11`, `page:12`). Cash flow statements for the nine months show repayments of $450.0 million and no proceeds from new long-term debt (`Q3 10-Q page:7`); the revolver was borrowed and repaid at 65.0 during the period. For use of proceeds and liquidity effect, the repayments were funded from operating cash flow of $606.0 million over nine months and reduced cash by little (cash $356.5 million against $360.4 million at December 31, 2025). Earlier history that shaped the balance sheet: the CMC Materials acquisition closed in July 2022 and was financed under the July 2022 credit agreement amendment and indenture supplements listed as exhibits (`10-K page:5`, `page:97`); debt payments of $848.3 million against proceeds of $224.5 million in FY2024 and payments of $300.0 million in FY2025 came after the asset sales listed in the timeline (`10-K page:108`). The nature of the FY2024 long-term debt proceeds is not described in the pack beyond a third amendment of the term loan facility in 2024 (`10-K page:76`, `page:98`). The dividend declared on October 14, 2026 ($0.10 per share, payable November 18, 2026) is a subsequent event after the quarter end (`Q3 10-Q page:17`). Management's Capital Markets Day on November 9, 2026 is a future event after the as-of date and no content from it is available (`Q3 release page:1`).

### Reader summary

| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Leverage fell from 4.23x at FY2025 to 3.27x on an LTM Q3 2026 basis, with net debt over Adjusted EBITDA at 2.91x. | Less debt and higher earnings widen the cushion against a demand downturn. | Medium |

| LTM Q3 2026 free cash flow was $616.0 million and cash interest cover was 5.57x; the remaining notes carry about $161.3 million of annual coupons. | Debt service is well covered while volumes hold, and the floating-rate term loan is gone. | Medium |

| Cash is $356.5 million and the undrawn revolver is $750.0 million before letters of credit; $2,000.0 million, or 60.7% of par debt, matures in 2029. | Liquidity is ample and nothing is due before 2028, but the 2029 refinancing is concentrated. | Medium |

| 2026 margins are lifted by lower depreciation and tariff refunds; on unadjusted EBITDA, leverage is 3.36x rather than 3.27x. | Reported improvement overstates the run-rate somewhat, and covenant EBITDA may differ from Adjusted EBITDA. | Medium |
### Credit view

Entegris, Inc. is a cyclical, customer-concentrated supplier of semiconductor materials whose credit profile improved sharply in 2026 and is now adequate for its debt load. The strongest support is deleveraging with cash generation: total debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 3.27x on an LTM Q3 2026 basis against 4.23x for FY2025, the term loan has been repaid, the remaining USD 3,295.0 million of debt is fixed-rate notes, and nothing matures before 2028. The weakest point is the quality and durability of earnings: demand is volume-led from a few very large customers with no purchase commitments, and 2026 margins are helped by an accounting change and one-off refunds. What decides the outcome is whether advanced logic and memory fab demand holds through the 2028 to 2030 maturities. [CP-1 leverage data; CP-1A operating model]
### Key findings

The first finding is that Entegris, Inc. has deleveraged on both sides of the ratio. Par debt fell to USD 3,295.0 million at September 26, 2026 from USD 3,745.0 million at December 31, 2025 through term loan repayment of USD 450.0 million, while LTM Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 1,008.2 million from USD 886.2 million in FY2025, so total debt over Adjusted EBITDA moved from 4.34x at FY2024 to 4.23x at FY2025 and 3.27x LTM Q3 2026, and net debt over Adjusted EBITDA from 3.99x to 3.82x to 2.91x. The mechanism is repayment from operating cash flow, which also removed floating-rate exposure, so the remaining debt service is fixed coupons of about USD 161.3 million a year and cash interest cover is 5.57x. [CP-1 leverage and interest cover data, debt schedule]

The second finding is that the cash generation behind this is strong but partly timing-supported. LTM free cash flow after capital spending was USD 616.0 million, equal to 18.7% of par debt, helped by capital spending of USD 182.0 million LTM against USD 299.2 million in FY2025 and by a working-capital inflow from payables and incentive accruals that the filings describe as timing. If capital spending returns toward the roughly USD 250.0 million planned in the annual report, or payables normalise, free cash flow would fall. [CP-1 financials and cash flow quality]

The third finding is that liquidity is ample and the maturity profile is back-ended but concentrated. Cash of USD 356.5 million plus the undrawn USD 750.0 million revolver gives USD 1,106.5 million before letters of credit, which are not supplied, and the revolver runs to April 29, 2031. Maturities are nil to 2027, USD 400.0 million in 2028, USD 2,000.0 million in 2029 (60.7% of par debt, including the USD 1,600.0 million secured notes) and USD 895.0 million in 2030, so refinancing risk sits in 2029 and depends on market access then. Only USD 58.3 million of the cash is held in the U.S. [CP-1 liquidity and debt maturities]

The fourth finding is that business risk is the weak side of the credit. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company was 16% of FY2025 net sales and the top ten customers were 50%; customers provide non-binding forecasts and no long-term purchase commitments. In Q3 2026 net sales rose 24.6% year on year, mainly on volume, but sales to Equipment and Engineering customers rose 66.8% against 19.3% for fabs, so part of the growth follows equipment shipments, which are more cyclical. A volume reversal would hit operating leverage first and then cash flow and leverage. [CP-1A operating model]

The fifth finding is that reported 2026 profitability flatters the run-rate. Depreciation was USD 55.6 million lower over nine months 2026 from a change in useful lives, and USD 8.3 million of tariff refunds helped Q3 2026 gross margin, though both are excluded from or neutral to Adjusted EBITDA. Adjusted EBITDA is management-defined; on unadjusted EBITDA, total leverage is 3.36x LTM Q3 2026 against 3.27x, so definition risk is small today. Covenant EBITDA is not supplied: the first lien net leverage covenant of 5.20x, tested only when revolver utilisation exceeds a threshold that is not printed, cannot be compared with any ratio, and a purely illustrative first lien net leverage of 1.23x (secured notes less cash over Adjusted EBITDA) is not covenant headroom. [CP-1 definition review, covenants]

The sixth finding concerns creditor control. No sponsor, parent or controlling holder is identified, dividends are a steady USD 0.10 per share each quarter, there were no buybacks in FY2025, and the documented actions are debt repayment, so no extraction behaviour is documented. The legal capacity to add secured debt is wide in principle, with incremental amounts up to the greater of USD 1.1 billion or 100% of EBITDA, and the financing documents, guarantor list and ratings are not supplied, so structural priority and any creditor-protection conclusion are left open. [CP-1A governance and capital allocation]
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Debt reduction with falling leverage is a documented fact: total debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 3.27x LTM Q3 2026, down from 4.34x at FY2024, with all remaining debt fixed-rate notes and no maturity before 2028 (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 leverage data and debt schedule). Cash generation is strong: LTM free cash flow of USD 616.0 million exceeds the sum of the roughly USD 161.3 million of annual note coupons and LTM dividends of USD 61.3 million, which is USD 222.6 million, by USD 393.4 million (Analyst Interpretation of CP-1 cash flow figures; the coupon figure excludes revolver fees). Liquidity of USD 1,106.5 million before letters of credit, with no facility expiring within twelve months, gives room to absorb a downturn (Documentary Fact for the inputs; the sum excludes unsupplied letters of credit). The business is embedded in customer processes through recurring consumables and no platform exceeds 3% of net sales, which management describes as supporting revenue that is predominantly unit-driven or recurring (Management Language; basis CP-1A operating model). Capital allocation is creditor-friendly on documented actions: debt repayment, steady dividends and no repurchases, with no sponsor (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A governance).

Weaknesses. Revenue is concentrated and uncommitted: one customer is 16% of FY2025 sales and ten customers are 50%, with no long-term purchase commitments (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A customers). Demand is cyclical and the recent growth leans on equipment-linked categories, which may reverse (Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1A end markets). Earnings quality needs care: depreciation was reduced by an accounting estimate change, tariff refunds were one-off, Adjusted EBITDA is management-defined and covenant EBITDA is unknown (Documentary Fact for the items; Analyst Interpretation for the effect). Refinancing is concentrated in 2029, at USD 2,000.0 million or 60.7% of par debt (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 debt maturities). Supply and trade exposure is real: single-source inputs, 26% of Q3 2026 sales to Taiwan and flat sales to China (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A operating model). Contract, covenant, letter-of-credit, guarantor and rating evidence is Not supplied, so headroom, structural priority and market view cannot be assessed (Insufficient Information; the missing items would decide covenant and structural conclusions).
### Credit assessment
| Item | Content | Category | Confidence |

| Fundamental credit view | Improving and adequate for the debt load; cyclical and customer-concentrated business risk offset by falling leverage, strong free cash flow and ample liquidity | Analyst Interpretation | Medium |

| Thesis | Entegris, Inc. can service and refinance its fixed-rate notes from cash flow if semiconductor volumes hold, and the 2029 maturity is the point at which the 2026 deleveraging is tested | Analyst Interpretation | Medium |

| Why not higher confidence | Management-defined Adjusted EBITDA, no covenant ratio, no letters of credit, no guarantor list, no ratings, customer concentration only to FY2025 | Insufficient Information | Not applicable |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Demand reversal in advanced logic, memory and fab construction | Volume falls with fab utilisation and equipment shipments; operating leverage works in reverse; customers can cancel or delay without commitment | Lower Adjusted EBITDA raises leverage from 3.27x and cuts interest cover from 5.57x; cash flow supports repayment less | Material |

| Customer and regional concentration | TSMC 16% of FY2025 sales, top ten 50%, Taiwan 26% of Q3 2026 sales; export controls, tariffs or cross-strait events affect several customers together | Tail risk to cash flow that leverage ratios do not show | Material |

| 2029 refinancing concentration | USD 2,000.0 million, 60.7% of par debt, matures in 2029, of which USD 1,600.0 million is secured notes | Refinancing depends on market access and earnings at that time; the revolver to 2031 gives a bridge, though its availability is shown before letters of credit | Material |

| Earnings quality and definition | Lower depreciation, tariff refunds and management-defined Adjusted EBITDA; covenant definition not supplied | Reported leverage may be better than a lender definition; headroom untested | Minor |

| Unknown contract terms | Covenant threshold, letters of credit, guarantors, incremental debt capacity of the greater of USD 1.1 billion or 100% of EBITDA | Secured debt can be added in principle, diluting existing claims; structural priority cannot be mapped | Material |
| Supply interruption | Single-source membranes, resins, abrasives and petroleum coke; slow re-qualification | Shipment shortfalls or cost increases hit margins | Minor |
### Monitoring posture

Treat the credit as improving but unconfirmed until the financing documents and covenant certificate are seen. Watch the fourth-quarter 2026 outturn against management's outlook (sales of USD 1,025 million to USD 1,055 million and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 315 million to USD 329 million, a management expectation, not a fact), the capital spending run-rate, the equipment-linked share of sales, any update to customer concentration, and the November 9, 2026 Capital Markets Day, which falls after the as-of date and is not evidence here.
## Calculations

Every figure above is a CP-1 or CP-1A value repeated unchanged, except the sums shown below: leverage ratios, cover, free cash flow, liquidity, maturities, concentration shares and the unadjusted EBITDA leverage of 3.36x. One simple sum is made: annual note coupons of USD 161.3 million plus LTM dividends of USD 61.3 million is USD 222.6 million, and LTM free cash flow of USD 616.0 million less USD 222.6 million is USD 393.4 million.

Pass to the evidence trace review (CP-5). It should test that each figure in this handoff matches the CP-1 and CP-1A values it repeats (leverage 3.27x, 2.91x and 4.23x, cover 5.57x, liquidity USD 1,106.5 million, 2029 maturity USD 2,000.0 million and 60.7%, free cash flow USD 616.0 million), that the Management Language rows are tagged as such, that no covenant headroom, sponsor, rating or recovery conclusion is stated, and that the illustrative first lien net leverage figure is never read as covenant headroom.
